references.text: Describes how touching a creeping thing (שֶׁרֶץ) makes a person unclean, expanding on the background of the uncleanness mentioned in Leviticus 22:5.
Lists specific creeping things that make a person unclean by touch, directly relating to the uncleanness from שֶׁרֶץ in this verse.
Refers to uncleanness from touching unclean things and human uncleanness, paralleling the two types of uncleanness mentioned in 22:5.
Describes uncleanness from touching a dead body, which is a form of human uncleanness (טֻמְאָה) referred to in the verse.
Explains that uncleanness is transmitted by touch, and the unclean person remains unclean until evening, relevant for the priests' state of purity.
Deals with uncleanness from touching an unclean person, illustrating בְאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא־לוֹ in the verse.
Provides context for priestly uncleanness through contact with the dead, part of the human uncleannesses priests must avoid.
Continues directly from verse 5 and describes the consequence of the uncleanness and the cleansing process for the priest.
